differential.name: Chronic pre-existing hypertension with super-imposed pre-eclampsia (hypertensive disorder of pregnancy)

supporting_evidence.finding: Stage 2 hypertension (149/98) in a pregnant patient on ACE inhibitor

differential.reasoning: Severe hypertension in pregnancy raises concern for superimposed pre-eclampsia, especially when chronic hypertension is present. Lack of proteinuria data is a limitation, but the clinical picture and risk factors prioritize this diagnosis.

differential.name: ACE inhibitor–induced renal hypoperfusion with secondary hypertension

supporting_evidence.finding: Contraindicated ACE inhibitor use during pregnancy
Borderline rise in BUN without creatinine data

differential.reasoning: ACE inhibitors can cause reduced renal perfusion in the fetus and mother, potentially worsening hypertension. Absence of definitive renal function labs weakens certainty.

differential.name: Metabolic syndrome contributing to gestational hypertension and endothelial dysfunction

supporting_evidence.finding: Chronic hypertension and obesity data missing (BMI unavailable)

differential.reasoning: Components of metabolic syndrome (insulin resistance, dyslipidemia) can exacerbate hypertension in pregnancy. Missing anthropometric data limits full assessment.

differential.name: Gestational diabetes mellitus
differential.reasoning: Prediabetes raises risk for GDM, but no glucose tolerance test results are available, making this a less certain contributor.

differential.name: Chronic anemia (iron-deficiency or anemia of chronic disease)
differential.reasoning: Anemia can contribute to high-output circulatory state and platelet activation, potentially influencing hypertension severity. Etiology remains undefined.

differential.name: Antiphospholipid syndrome / systemic lupus erythematosus (autoimmune thrombophilia)

supporting_evidence.finding: Elevated platelet distribution width (PDW 268.5 fL) without platelet count

differential.reasoning: Abnormal platelet indices raise the possibility of an underlying autoimmune thrombophilia, but no serologic testing is available.

primary_diagnosis: Chronic pre-existing hypertension with super-imposed pre-eclampsia (hypertensive disorder of pregnancy)
clinical_reasoning_summary: The pregnant patient presents with severe, uncontrolled hypertension while on a contraindicated ACE inhibitor. Chronic hypertension combined with the acute rise in blood pressure makes superimposed pre‑eclampsia the most urgent and probable diagnosis, despite missing proteinuria data. ACE‑inhibitor induced renal hypoperfusion remains a plausible secondary contributor given the drug exposure and early renal lab changes. Metabolic syndrome and pre‑diabetes further predispose to hypertensive disorders, while gestational diabetes, chronic anemia, and possible autoimmune thrombophilia are less certain but still relevant differentials.
unresolved_findings: Markedly high PDW (268.5 fL) without platelet count
Low‑normal RBC (4.1 ×10⁶/µL) without iron studies or vitamin B12/folate
No serum creatinine/eGFR or urine protein/creatinine ratio
No documented prenatal vitamin or iron supplementation
Absence of fetal growth assessments or ultrasound data
recommended_workup: Serum creatinine, eGFR, and BUN to assess renal function
Urine protein‑to‑creatinine ratio or 24‑hour urine protein for pre‑eclampsia evaluation
Blood pressure monitoring with ambulatory cuff
Fetal ultrasound with growth parameters and Doppler studies
Complete lipid panel and calculation of BMI
Iron studies (serum ferritin, transferrin saturation) and vitamin B12/folate levels
Oral glucose tolerance test to confirm or exclude gestational diabetes
Antiphospholipid antibody panel (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, beta‑2 glycoprotein I) and ANA for autoimmune screening
Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4) to rule out hypothyroidism
